Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for opening bank accounts and accessing financial services
Comments: The CNIB is required for opening a bank account and accessing financial services in Burkina Faso. Per Tanager International (2023): 'Voting in elections, holding a job, opening a bank account — all require an identity card.' CNIB is accepted but ownership is not 100% mandatory for all financial transactions.
revision_notes: Original cited sources checked: Tanager (2023) confirms a national identity card is a 'must' for opening a bank account in Burkina Faso, which supports a stronger code than the one assigned; the Smile ID page names KYC/AML regulators but does not itself address whether ID is mandatory for account opening. Fresh checks of published account-opening requirements at two Burkinabe banks (UBA Burkina Faso; IB Bank Burkina, 2026) confirm that a valid CNIB or passport is a required document. BCEAO's regional customer-identification instruction (n°003-03-2025, 18 March 2025), binding on all UEMOA financial institutions including Burkina Faso, mandates identity verification as part of KYC/CDD. Combined, the evidence supports Mandatory rather than Accepted-but-not-mandatory. Value code revised from 2 to 3.
revised_comments: A valid national identity document (CNIB) or passport is a mandatory requirement for opening a bank account in Burkina Faso. Commercial banks (e.g. UBA Burkina Faso, IB Bank Burkina) list a valid CNIB or passport among the compulsory documents for account opening, and BCEAO's regional instruction on customer identification and KYC (Instruction n°003-03-2025, effective across the UEMOA/WAEMU zone) requires financial institutions to verify client identity as part of due diligence. The CNIB is similarly required for voting, formal employment and SIM card registration, reflecting its role as Burkina Faso's primary identification credential.
